learning_objective: 🎯 Understand quantities that have both magnitude AND direction, and learn how they interact in space using dot and cross products!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A scalar is just a number (like 5 kg or 10 meters). A vector is a number WITH a direction (like 10 meters heading North). We represent vectors with little arrows over their letters.
A unit vector has a magnitude of exactly 1. The vectors $\hat{i}$, $\hat{j}$, and $\hat{k}$ are the bosses of the x, y, and z axes. They help us write any vector in 3D space.
Multiplying two vectors to get a standard number. It is calculated using the cosine of the angle between them. If two vectors are perfectly perpendicular (90°), their dot product is exactly 0!
Multiplying two vectors to get a BRAND NEW third vector that sticks straight out, perfectly perpendicular to both original vectors. This uses the sine of the angle.

fun_activity.title: 🗺️ The Vector Treasure Hunt
fun_activity.instructions: Stand in the middle of a room (Origin). Walk 3 steps Forward (3i), 4 steps Right (4j), and point 2 steps Up (2k). You just physically plotted the position vector $3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$!

exam_tips: 📌 Proving vectors are perpendicular? Show $A \cdot B = 0$. Proving they are parallel? Show $A \times B = 0$ (or that one is a scalar multiple of the other).
📌 To find a unit vector in the direction of vector A, simply divide the vector by its own magnitude: $\hat{A} = A / |A|$.
📌 Use determinants to quickly and accurately calculate the Cross Product without confusing the i, j, k signs.
quick_recap: ⭐ Vectors need both size (magnitude) and a compass heading (direction).
⭐ Dot Product results in a number; Cross Product results in a new perpendicular vector.
⭐ $\hat{i}$, $\hat{j}$, $\hat{k}$ represent the x, y, and z axes.
